title: Studying Redhead: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in Martian Remote Sensing
abstract: A scientific computing framework investigating whether statistical and unsupervised machine learning methods can identify interpretable unusual surface patterns in Martian orbital observations. The project distinguishes observed surface characteristics from observational artefacts and model-generated interpretations.
content:
## Research Motivation

Planetary remote sensing produces extensive observations whose interpretation requires reliable data processing and scientifically defensible computational methods.

## Research Question

To what extent can statistical and unsupervised machine learning methods identify unusual Martian surface patterns while distinguishing genuine surface characteristics from observational and preprocessing artefacts?

## Current Engineering Progress

The existing infrastructure includes modular raster ingestion, geospatial coordinate transformations, raster tiling, normalization, exploratory spatial data analysis, logging, exception handling and automated pipeline orchestration.

The development handoff reports 41 passing automated tests, 87% combined code coverage and three successful pipeline executions. These are engineering validation results, not planetary research findings. Authentic Martian observations have not yet been integrated.

## Planned Scientific Datasets

- CTX orbital imagery for morphological and textural analysis.
- MOLA elevation products for regional topographic context.
- Published Martian geological maps and crater catalogues for interpretation and proxy evaluation.
- Optional CRISM products for future spectral investigations.

## Proposed Experimental Methodology

Begin with a bounded Martian study region. Statistical and classical image-processing baselines will precede investigation of Isolation Forest, PCA and convolutional or variational autoencoders. Multimodal fusion requires scientifically appropriate spatial alignment.

## Evaluation Protocol

Geographically separated data partitions, reference-based proxy tasks, sensitivity analysis, false-positive assessment and uncertainty estimation will support comparative evaluation.

## Scientific Visualization

Georeferenced anomaly maps and interactive terrain visualization will communicate findings after scientific validation.

## Current Limitations

Existing terrestrial reference datasets and synthetic fixtures are used only for engineering validation. No geological discoveries or validated planetary anomaly detection results are currently claimed.
